closurePoint: Madison Falls parking area (washout beyond; NPS: 2 mi from US-101 to park boundary, 9.6 mi to road end)
footBikeAllowed: Yes: pedestrians, bicycles and leashed dogs. Bikes not allowed past Boulder Creek trailhead.
reopening: No date published. NPS road page entry last updated 2021-05-07; no reopening notice found as of 2026-10-29.

trailheads.name: Whiskey Bend
trailheads.derivation: NPS trail conditions: adds about 6.5 mi. A third-party source says 6.2; NPS figure used. No source gives the gain of the road walk.

trailheads.name: Boulder Creek
trailheads.derivation: NPS trail conditions: adds about 8 mi (Hot Springs a further 2.4 mi on foot). Gain not given by any source.

sources.says: Elwha closed to vehicles beyond Madison Falls parking due to washout; adds ~6.5 mi to Whiskey Bend and ~8 mi to Boulder Creek.
Olympic Hot Springs Road closed to vehicles by washout; open to pedestrians, bikes, leashed dogs; Madison Falls lot open, limited turnaround.
Park alert mirror (search summary only): Whiskey Bend Road closed to vehicles by washouts; walk/bike reaches trailhead.

disagreements: Whiskey Bend walk quoted as 6.2 mi (third-party) vs 6.5 mi (NPS). Start of closure variously given as 2017, 2021 or Sept 2024; the NPS pages agree it is closed now. Route texts say 6.2-8.0 mi.
statusSentence: As of late October 2026 the Elwha road stays closed to vehicles at the Madison Falls parking area because of a washout, with walkers and cyclists allowed through and no reopening date set.

closurePoint: Washout outside the park boundary, 6.5 mi by road from Dosewallips Campground (washed out since 2002/2003)
footBikeAllowed: Yes: pedestrian and bicycle traffic only.
reopening: None published; no repair planned in any source found.

trailheads.name: Dosewallips Ranger Station / Dosewallips River Trail
trailheads.derivation: NPS Dosewallips River Trail page: 5.5 mi from road closure to the ranger station. NPS pages also say the washout adds 6.5 mi to a trip (to campground/road end). The 5.5 vs 6.5 gap is unreconciled. Gain: page gives 2,650 ft at the ranger station but nothing at the closure, so the road-walk gain is unknown.

sources.says: 5.5 mi from road closure to ranger station; road washed out, adds 6.5 mi hiking.
Closed to vehicles, washout outside park boundary 6.5 mi from the campground; pedestrians and bikes only.

disagreements: 5.5 mi (closure to ranger station) vs 6.5 mi (closure to campground/road end) on NPS pages; route texts use 5.0-6.6. Closure date given as 2002 (most sources) vs 2017 (NPS road-page stamp).
statusSentence: As of late October 2026 the Dosewallips River Road remains closed to vehicles at a washout outside the park, with the park reporting 5.5 miles on foot or bike from the closure to the ranger station and no reopening planned.

road: Monte Cristo Road (Mountain Loop Highway beyond Barlow Pass)
footBikeAllowed: Yes: foot and bike; walkers go around the gate.
reopening: None; closed to motors since the 2003 and 2006 Sauk River floods. Separate winter gating of Barlow to Bedal also applies.

trailheads.name: Monte Cristo townsite
trailheads.derivation: WTA: 4.0 mi each way along the closed road, 700 ft gain (Barlow 2,360 ft, high point 2,800 ft).

trailheads.name: Glacier Basin (via townsite)
trailheads.derivation: Road portion same as the townsite. Glacier Basin round trip from Barlow is 12.0 mi and 2,159 ft gain (WTA), so the trail beyond the townsite is about 2 mi one way (derived).

trailheads.name: Weden Creek (Gothic Basin) trail
trailheads.derivation: Route text only: about 1 mi up the closed road. Not independently confirmed.

sources.says: 4 mi to townsite on closed road, 8.0 mi round trip, 700 ft gain; 2003 and 2006 floods.
Glacier Basin 12.0 mi round trip, 2,159 ft gain; start behind gate.
Loop open Deer Creek to Barlow Pass; Barlow to Bedal still closed.

disagreements: One source puts the townsite 4.5 mi from the highway (Cascade Hiker) vs 4.0 (WTA). Glacier Basin round trip ranges 12.0-13.4 mi across sources.
statusSentence: As of late October 2026 the Monte Cristo road is closed to vehicles at Barlow Pass and has been since the 2003 and 2006 floods, so the townsite is a 4-mile walk or bike ride with about 700 feet of gain.

closurePoint: Locked gate at the Dingford Creek trailhead (about 18 mi from North Bend); washout at MP 17.3 listed 2026-07-01
footBikeAllowed: Yes: bikes and walkers pass the gate.
reopening: None for the gate (gated since 2007). Forest Service says repairs to several roads are planned over summer 2026 and 2027; the MP 17.3 washout has no stated fix date.

trailheads.name: Old road end / Dutch Miller Gap trailhead
trailheads.derivation: Route text (one source only): about 7.5 mi of closed road from the Dingford gate to the old road end. No second source.

trailheads.name: Hardscrabble Creek / Hardscrabble Lakes boot path
trailheads.derivation: Starts from the road end, so the same road walk. A Mountaineers report gives 8.3 mi on trail from Dingford to a camp near Hardscrabble Creek; that is not a road distance.

sources.says: FSR 56 road washout at MP 17.3; repairs planned this summer and next.
Locked gate at Dingford Creek trailhead; bikes allowed beyond.
Locked gate at the Dingford parking lot, no motor vehicles; last miles very rough.

disagreements: A July 2026 crowd entry says the road is clear while the Forest Service lists a washout at MP 17.3. Route texts use 7.0 vs 7.5 mi. Where the washout sits relative to the gate is unresolved.
statusSentence: As of late October 2026 vehicles stop at the locked gate at the Dingford Creek trailhead, with walkers and bikes allowed on about 7.5 miles of closed road beyond it and a washout at mile 17.3 still listed.

closurePoint: Major washout about 0.8 mi (4WD) to 1.7 mi (~2,600 ft) up the spur off Chilliwack Lake Road; no gate
reopening: None; no BC notice found. Unmaintained and varies year to year.

trailheads.name: Depot Creek trail / Monument 65 (border)
trailheads.derivation: Washout reported at 0.8 mi (SummitPost summary), 1.6 mi and 1.7 mi (route texts, 2004 report). Walk from washout to border: route text says about 3.2 mi on one route and about 45 minutes (0.8 hr) on another. These disagree, so no single figure is given.

sources.says: Progress halted after 1.7 mi by a major washout (search summary).
4WD may reach a washout about 0.8 mi past parking (search summary only; page returned 403).
Unsigned turnoff 200 yards before the Depot Creek bridge; walk road, left and right at junctions (search summary).

disagreements: Washout at 0.8, 1.6 or 1.7 mi depending on source; nothing dated 2025 or 2026 found. Walk from washout to border 3.2 mi vs about 45 min.
statusSentence: As of late October 2026 no current report was found on Depot Creek Road, which has long ended at a washout roughly 1 to 2 miles in, so plan to walk the old road grade from there.

closurePoint: Was closed at the Glacier Creek bridge (MP 3.0) from 2026-06-30 for repairs
footBikeAllowed: n/a (reopened). During the closure pedestrians and cyclists could pass at the engineer's discretion.
reopening: Reopened 2026-08-20 after repairs. The 'through end of October' text is outdated.

trailheads.name: Heliotrope Ridge
trailheads.derivation: Road open to the trailhead, so no closure walk applies. Grouse Butte Road FS 36 stays closed at MP 0.6, a separate road.

sources.says: Forest Service announced repairs complete; hikers and climbers can again drive to Heliotrope Ridge trailhead.

sources.date: 2026 (headline seen in search results; body not read)
sources.says: Title: Forest Service has opened Glacier Creek Road.

disagreements: Route texts saying closed through end of October 2026 are stale. Only one article body was read; the official release body was not opened.
statusSentence: Glacier Creek Road reopened to vehicles on 20 August 2026 after flood repairs, so as of late October 2026 the Heliotrope Ridge trailhead can be driven to.

footBikeAllowed: Yes: foot and bike pass the gate.
reopening: No date published; closed until further notice for maintenance (Oct 2026). A hiking guide says typical reopening is around July 4.

trailheads.name: Cascade Pass / Boston Basin
trailheads.derivation: Road is 23 mi from Marblemount to its end and the closure is at MP 20, so about 3 mi (inferred). Gain of 1,500 ft comes from one route text only.

sources.says: Closed at MP 20 (Eldorado) until further notice for road maintenance; foot and bike allowed.
Closed at MP 20; road runs 23 mi from Marblemount.
Closure from Oct 13 through winter; typical reopening about July 4 (search summary).

disagreements: Route texts say the 2026 closure began in June from flood or landslide damage near MP 18; a July WTA report says the gate was expected to open, so the summer closure ended and a new maintenance closure began in October. Route texts use 3.0 vs 4.0 mi.
statusSentence: As of late October 2026 the Cascade River Road is closed to vehicles at the Eldorado gate at mile 20 for maintenance, about 3 miles short of the Cascade Pass trailhead, with walkers and bikes allowed and no reopening date.

closurePoint: MP 3.7 to the junction with FR 27 (road failure near mile 4)
footBikeAllowed: Unclear: the Forest Service order bans being on the road and does not separate foot or bike use; a 2024 trip report describes biking it.
reopening: None; the alert lists no end date. Forest Service release of 2026-07-01 plans repairs in summer 2026 and 2027.

trailheads.name: White Chuck River trailhead (old road end)
trailheads.derivation: No source states the road length from the closure to the trailhead. A 2024 report (search summary; page returned 403) describes about 2 mi past the washout plus 4.5 mi up the closed road, which is not reconciled.

sources.says: FR 23 closed from MP 3.7 to FR 27 for flood damage; order bans being on the road except exempt persons.
Temporary closure MP 3.7 to FR 27; repairs planned this summer and next.
Total road failure at mile 4; Crystal Creek trailhead not reachable by vehicle.

disagreements: The order text runs through 2025-12-31 unless rescinded, yet the alert shows no end date and was updated mid-2026. Whether walking or biking is permitted is unresolved. The 2024 bike report is not current.
statusSentence: As of late October 2026 White Chuck River Road is closed at mile 3.7 after flood damage with no reopening date, and the distance on to the old trailhead is not confirmed.
